root.name: Vienna Gambit, with Max Lange Defense: Cunningham Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. f4 exf4 4. Nf3 Be7

overview: The Vienna Gambit reaches 3.f4 exf4 4.Nf3 Be7, the Cunningham-style move which blocks the e-file and threatens ...Bh4+. White usually develops with Bc4 and castles, then pushes d4 and e5. Black keeps the pawn and counters in the centre. Play is open and tactical.

white_ideas.idea: Play Bc4 and castle, then d4 and e5
Hit f7 with Bc4 and Ng5

black_ideas.idea: Keep the f4 pawn and play ...Bh4+ or ...d5

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after d4 with e4/f4 against ...e7/c6

character.notes: Open game with attacking chances for White and counterplay for Black.

gambit.notes: White gave up f4 and Black can hold on to it.

soundness.notes: The gambit is considered playable and the Cunningham line is sound for both sides.

approach.notes: The Vienna Gambit is a respectable choice.

level.notes: Specific responses to ...Bh4+ and ...d5 must be known.

character.reason: White gives a pawn for an attack and Black can punish slips.

gambit.reason: White gave up f4 and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: The gambit is a respected line.

structure.reason: The centre opens early and pieces get lines.

approach.reason: It is a respectable choice at every level.

plans.reason: White develops fast and aims at f7.
